articles.title: Thunkable Joins Florida’s 2026–27 CAPE Industry Certification Funding List

articles.summary: Vibe coding, a term coined by AI researcher Andrej Karpathy in 2025, means building software by telling AI what you want and refining it through conversation. For no-code builders, that's a big shift. Instead of assembling your app one block at a time, you can start with a description and let AI generate the screens, design, and logic for you. That means faster iteration and a lower barrier to getting your idea in front of real users. You're still in charge, though. You decide what your app should do, whether it truly serves your users, and whether it works on a real device before you ship it. With Thunkable's AI Builder, you can vibe code a native mobile app from the start. You can refine it with prompts, blocks, or code, test it on your phone, and publish it to the App Store or Google Play.
articles.title: How Vibe Coding Changed No-Code App Building

articles.summary: This summer, ~120 West Virginia high schoolers built roughly 80 real mobile apps using Thunkable through an AI education pilot backed by The Rockefeller Foundation and the state. The program drove hands-on AI/entrepreneurship learning, with 44% of participants reporting increased interest in starting their own businesses.
articles.title: West Virginia Students Build Real Apps With Thunkable

articles.summary: Thunkable is attending Futures Summit 2026 ("Human Skills in an Autonomous World") on September 9–10 at the Santa Clara Convention Center, joining 1,000+ educators and innovators. The team is excited to discuss AI/emerging tech in education, human skills alongside technical fluency, and preparing students for the workforce. Attendees can visit Thunkable's booth or book a live demo to build an app in three minutes.
articles.title: Thunkable Is Heading to Futures Summit 2026
